source.title: Certification of Machine Learning Models via Directional Sharpness
source.authors: Ge-Fei Tan; Adrià Gascón; Sarah Meiklejohn; Mariana Raykova

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the relation between sharpness measures and the training–test generalization gap with a different, dynamic sharpness measure; also compares this measure on models with training deviations.
record.gate_note: The study measures generalization gaps and sharpness, and reports separate benign/faulty distinguishability results. Table 4's membership-inference scores, runtime and ZKP cost estimates do not measure a version's named generalization behavior, so they are not rows. Cited results from prior work are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: Table 1 directly evaluates magnitude-aware worst-case sharpness against the generalization gap, using Jiang et al.'s gradient-ascent algorithm on 1,152 converged models. This bears on V7. Directional stability, deviation detection, and membership inference do not themselves measure V7's named relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that directional sharpness predicts empirical generalization gaps better than the tested static measures, detects specified training deviations, and enables efficient auditing and metric-based certification. Their certificates verify a metric predicate, not the true generalization gap or its relationship to the metric.
record.recipe_differences: Measures a dynamic sharpness trajectory using repeated stochastic SAM-style updates and compares it with static sharpness metrics; it does not reproduce the claim versions' interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Directional sharpness settings vary, including probe batch size and number of steps; the reported faulty-model ratios and gap correlations are tied to their stated datasets, optimizer grids, and deviation conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Directional sharpness correlates strongly with empirical generalization gaps, including Spearman correlations of 0.902 and 0.811.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic sharpness fluctuations along short stochastic optimization trajectories predict generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: Directional sharpness separates the reported benign/faulty pairs more strongly than static ASAM, including backdoor, shortcut, label-noise, quantization, and artifact conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directional sharpness can flag specified model defects despite nearly matched observed accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Directional sharpness yields membership-inference AUC 0.556 and accuracy 0.570.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-example directional sharpness can serve as a membership-inference score.

fits_no_version.finding: Directional sharpness correctly orders the SAM–SGD pair by reported gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic sharpness can distinguish generalization differences missed by static ASAM in this pair.

record.problems: The paper reports aggregate correlations over a selected grid of converged models, with no uncertainty estimates in the shown tables. Several deviation tests are benign/faulty model pairs with no reported replicate variation. The central V7 measure in the claim—magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance—is not tested; the study evaluates dynamic sharpness and static comparator metrics instead.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 reports runtime and correlation for probe configurations, but these overlap the correlation evidence in Table 1 and are not additional conditions on the named V7 behavior. Table 4 membership-inference results are not generalization-gap results and were not retained as version-bearing rows. ZKP cost estimates and other certification efficiency measures do not bear on the versions.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels versus natural-label held-out generalization and chance-level random-label performance.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Optimizer performance comparisons under specified tuning budgets; sweeping optimizers without reporting their held-out comparisons does not test this version.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Held-out effects of adding or removing dropout; the hyperparameter grid alone supplies no such comparison.

Ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; SVHN; an explicitly augmentation-free replication. Table 1 pools architectures and datasets rather than reporting within-family correlations separately. Comparable final training losses are not established for the SAM–SGD pair.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The central extraction error is denying that magnitude-aware worst-case sharpness was evaluated: Sections 4.5 and 5 explicitly identify this baseline and Jiang et al.'s algorithm. Dynamic stability and defect detection should not be counted as direct support for V7. No uncertainty estimates accompany the reported correlations or pair comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization versus generalization on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and removal of dropout/weight decay.

The study tests dynamic sharpness and static ASAM/worst-case sharpness as gap measures, but does not test the magnitude-aware perturbation-tolerance measure named in the version or compare it with the norm- and margin-based measures named there. Its sharpness-versus-gap results are correlational.
Removing influential memorized training examples and retraining.

source_check.correct: Separate the metrics. SAM: static ASAM 0.195, generalization gap 0.205; SGD: static ASAM 0.170, gap 0.273. The static ASAM ordering is reversed.
